name: Papaya soap

lead: Papaya soap is a bar soap that includes papaya, usually for gentle exfoliation and a brighter, more even-looking skin tone. Users apply it as a normal cleanser.
Papain, the enzyme in papaya, has wide commercial use in cosmetics, and its role in wound debridement is documented.

paras: It is lathered and rinsed in a regular washing routine; results are described by users over weeks.
In 2008 the FDA received reports of serious allergic reactions to topical papain products, and people allergic to latex may also be allergic to papaya.

studies.title: FERMENTED PAPAYA SOAP AND METHOD FOR PRODUCING THE SAME

angle.text: Users apply it as a regular cleanser for exfoliation and brightness. Claims about lightening come from product marketing and user reports.

lead: Papaya soap is a cleansing bar containing papaya extract, used by people hoping to exfoliate and lighten the appearance of skin.
Papaya is the source of papain, an enzyme collected from the fruit's latex and used commercially in cosmetics and, in ointments, for removing dead tissue from wounds.[1]

paras: The FDA received reports in 2008 of serious allergic reactions, including low blood pressure and rapid heart rate, to topical papain products; people allergic to latex may also be allergic to papaya.[1]
